:::{.phase-header}
# From Vibes to Variables
**3rd Edition --- Fall 2026**

A complete open textbook for research methods in mass communication. 14 chapters across 5 parts, designed for both undergraduate (MC 451) and graduate (MC 501) instruction.

[Read the Full Textbook](https://aura-lab-siue.github.io/v2v/){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg}
:::

---

:::{.callout-info}
## Preview Edition

This page previews the chapter structure and themes for the Fall 2026 (3rd) edition. The full textbook is available online and is updated regularly. The book ships in two audience profiles from one source: an **Undergraduate Edition** (MC 451 --- final piece: a Feature Article + Methodology Appendix) and the **Graduate Supplement, *Beyond Vibes*** (MC 501 --- final piece: a White Paper + Academic Conference Poster), which adds power analysis, pre-registration, two-coder reliability planning, and an audit-trail layer.
:::

---

## Part I: Foundation

*Chapters 1--3 build the habits and infrastructure every researcher needs before touching data.*

| Ch | Title | What You'll Learn |
|----|-------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Science of Storytelling** | How research questions emerge from curiosity and observation, and why methods are a form of disciplined storytelling |
| 2 | **The Open Workspace** | Setting up the open-source research workspace --- R, VS Code, Quarto, Git/GitHub, and the Methods Vault |
| 3 | **Knowing and Knowing Well** | Epistemology for researchers --- what makes a claim trustworthy: validity, reliability, and the logic of evidence |

---

## Part II: Planning

*Chapters 4--6 cover the decisions that shape a study before any data is collected.*

| Ch | Title | What You'll Learn |
|----|-------|-------------------|
| 4 | **Intelligence Gathering** | Finding and evaluating sources --- literature searching, media archives, and the librarian visit |
| 5 | **Theory as a Lens** | Choosing a theoretical framework and using it to focus your research questions |
| 6 | **The Prospectus** | Turning questions and theory into a concrete project plan (prospectus / research proposal) |

---

## Part III: Operationalization

*Chapters 7--9 move from planning to building the measurement tools of a content analysis.*

| Ch | Title | What You'll Learn |
|----|-------|-------------------|
| 7 | **Structured Listening** | Qualitative immersion in the class dataset --- observing, listening, and finding patterns |
| 8 | **From Vibes to Variables** | Turning qualitative observations into a quantitative codebook (concepts to variables) |
| 9 | **The Rulebook and First Workspace** | Coding decision rules, anchor examples, intercoder reliability, and your first project workspace |

---

## Part IV: Execution

*Chapters 10--12 run the content-analysis pipeline --- sampling through visualization --- hands-on in R.*

| Ch | Title | What You'll Learn |
|----|-------|-------------------|
| 10 | **The Sample** | Sampling strategy, sample size, selection, and pilot testing your codebook |
| 11 | **Wrangling the Data** [R] | Importing, diagnosing, cleaning, and exporting data in R with the tidyverse |
| 12 | **Visualizing the Narrative** [R] | Descriptive statistics, frequency tables, and publication-quality visualization with ggplot2 |

---

## Part V: Inference and Publication

*Chapters 13--14 bring the analysis to a decision and a finished, shareable research product.*

| Ch | Title | What You'll Learn |
|----|-------|-------------------|
| 13 | **Making the Call** [R] | Inferential statistics --- appropriate tests, effect sizes, significance, and APA-format reporting |
| 14 | **The One-Click Report** [R] | Assembling a Quarto report (PDF + website from one source) and publishing to GitHub Pages |

---

## About the Textbook

*From Vibes to Variables* is an open educational resource written by Dr. Alex P. Leith for research methods courses at SIUE. The 3rd edition (Fall 2026) restructures the book into 14 focused chapters across 5 parts, adds the R Workbook as a companion, and integrates with the [Methods Vault](methods-vault.qmd) and the **`v2v` R package** (`remotes::install_github("aura-lab-siue/v2v-r")`).

The class dataset ships inside the `v2v` package: **`twitch_chat_sample`** (~35,000 public Twitch IRC chat messages from 50 channels, Nov 18--24 2018) and **`twitch_streams_sample`** (~32,000 concurrent stream snapshots for the same channels). Students load them with `twitch_chat()` and `twitch_streams()`, and the package's helpers (`clean_dates()`, `join_chat_streams()`, `sample_messages()`, `reliability()`, `run_chi_square()`, `run_t_test()`, `theme_v2v()`, `new_portfolio()`, `deploy_portfolio()`, `setup()`) are introduced chapter by chapter.

The textbook is free, open-access, and published via [GitHub Pages](https://aura-lab-siue.github.io/v2v/).
